metrics.label: Brent crude
metrics.blurb: The global benchmark price for crude oil. Most oil cargoes price off it.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas
metrics.blurb: Europe's benchmark gas price, set in the Netherlands.
metrics.fallback: read from the daily European gas report

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas
metrics.blurb: The US benchmark gas price, set in Louisiana.

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)
metrics.blurb: Price of coal delivered into northwest Europe. A dry bulk demand signal.
metrics.fallback: CNBC lists ICE API2 but returns it undated; nothing else free publishes it.
metrics.source: ICE API2 Rotterdam Coal via CNBC

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil
metrics.blurb: A refined product price that tracks what bunker fuel costs.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote (ULSD heating oil front-month)

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline
metrics.blurb: US gasoline price. Strong margins here pull product tankers west.

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding dry bulk freight futures. A rough daily read on bulker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Dry Bulk Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.
metrics.source: Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: VLCC (TD3C, AG→China)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 2m-barrel crude tanker on the Arabian Gulf to China run. The most quoted tanker rate in the world.

rates.label: Suezmax (TD20, W.Africa→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 1m-barrel crude tanker from West Africa to Europe.

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 600k-barrel crude tanker on a short North Sea haul — the route closest to Norwegian crude exports.

rates.label: LR2 (TC1, AG→Japan)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a large product tanker carrying clean refined products.

rates.label: MR (TC2, Rotterdam→NY)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker on the transatlantic gasoline run.

rates.label: MR (TC14, US Gulf→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker carrying clean products east across the Atlantic.

rates.label: Capesize 5TC
rates.blurb: Average daily earnings of a 180,000t bulker across five iron ore and coal routes.

rates.label: LNG (BLNG1, Australia→Japan)
rates.blurb: Spot charter rate for a standard LNG carrier on the Pacific route.

rates.label: LNG (BLNG2, US Gulf→Continent)

rates.label: LNG (BLNG3, US Gulf→Japan)
rates.blurb: The long-haul LNG route. It pays more than BLNG2 because the voyage is far longer, so the gap between them tracks the TTF–JKM arbitrage.

brief.text:
The only figures that refreshed this morning are bunker prices — the fuel ships burn — and they are all lower. VLSFO (very low sulphur fuel oil, the standard main-engine fuel for most ships) was quoted today at 763.50 USD/t in Rotterdam, down 31.00 or 3.9%, and 814.00 USD/t in Houston, down 36.50 or 4.3%, while Singapore slipped 16.00 to 1,003.50 USD/t (-1.6%) and Fujairah just 2.00 to 991.50 USD/t (-0.2%). For anyone fixing a voyage, that matters directly: cheaper Atlantic bunkers lift the owner's net daily earnings on the same freight rate, and the gap between a West and East stem has widened again. Nothing in today's headlines explains the fall, and the crude benchmarks have not refreshed, so the data here does not show why.

No benchmark crude or freight figure is today's. Brent stood at 117.19 USD/bbl and WTI at 103.88 on Friday 30 October, with a Brent-WTI spread of 13.31; gasoline at 3.05 USD/gal is nine sessions old and did not refresh. On the dry side, Monday 2 November readings showed the Baltic Dry Index at 2,648 points, down 2.4%, with the Capesize index (biggest bulkers, mainly iron ore and coal) at 3,963, up 237 or 6.4% against 26 October, while Panamax was 1,874 (-0.8%) and Supramax 1,856 (-0.5%). Tanker TCE — time charter equivalent, the daily earnings a voyage rate converts into — was reported on Sunday 1 November at 1,345,710 USD/day for VLCC AG-China, 466,000 for Aframax North Sea-UKC, 288,700 for LR2 AG-Japan, 73,500 for MR US Gulf-UKC and 16,600 for MR Rotterdam-New York. None of these moved today; they are background.

Today's headlines added nothing to the running stories. The attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz, the Black Sea drone strikes, Arabian Gulf congestion and transit counts, Russia's diesel export ban, the Los Angeles-Long Beach security-worker standoff and Chinese patrols off Taiwan are all unchanged on this data, not resolved. Company news was earnings and contracts: Wallenius Wilhelmsen's USD 700m auto deal and USD 1bn equipment contracts, KCC's Q3, Scorpio Tankers' Q3 and dividend increase, and a Dorian LPG irregular dividend.

Watch two things. First, the 4 November deadline extension in the US West Coast labour dispute, which is tomorrow and covers a large share of US import capacity. Second, whether Baltic and crude prints refresh, since almost everything above is one to nine sessions old.

storylines.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continued into November, with a tanker hit off Saudi Arabia and an offshore tug struck in Hormuz on 1 November, and an LNG carrier attacked near the Strait.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on hulls raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting crude and product tanker earnings.

storylines.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea this month.
storylines.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz recorded six VLCC transits on Oct 25, the most since Oct 17, with one VLCC through Bab al-Mandab on each of Oct 24 and Oct 25. Vessel waiting remains elevated across the Arabian Gulf, with 265 dry bulk vessels waiting as of 28 October and Fujairah holding 28% of them.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia's government has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving 250 security workers threatens to freeze operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals after a 4 November deadline extension, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond on Friday over arms shipments through their ports.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Chinese patrols off Taiwan's east coast
storylines.what: Taiwan's Coast Guard says China's Coast Guard is harassing shipping with a patrol off Taiwan's east coast and asserting what Taipei calls a fictional jurisdiction, and has sent its own ships in response.
storylines.why_it_matters: Interference with commercial traffic near a major East Asian routing corridor can affect transit decisions, insurance and schedules for ships serving North Asia.
